evals.name: vague-description
evals.prompt: Review .opencode/skills/cache-cleanup/SKILL.md. Its description is 'Helps with code.'
evals.expected_output: A major finding under criterion (c): the description does not say what the skill does or when to use it. The review proposes a description with concrete trigger phrases and a not-ready verdict.
expectations: The review names criterion (c) and marks the description as a major finding.
The review says the description does not name what the skill does.
The review proposes concrete trigger phrases from the skill's purpose, not a generic word.
The verdict is not ready, and it agrees with the finding.

evals.name: false-git-example
evals.prompt: Review this skill. It says `git branch feature/x-probe` cannot exist beside `feature/x`.
evals.expected_output: The reviewer runs the example in a scratch repository, finds that the two names coexist, and reports a major reliability finding with the real conflict shape, a name that is a directory prefix of another.
expectations: The reviewer runs the git command before judging the claim.
The review reports that the two branch names coexist.
The review explains the real conflict shape: a name that is a directory prefix, such as feature/x/probe.
The finding is major and belongs to reliability.

evals.name: bloated-body
evals.prompt: Review this skill: its body is 900 lines, including a 400-line table of vendor limits that only one section uses.
evals.expected_output: A context-efficiency finding: the body loads on every trigger, so the vendor table moves to references/ and the skill points at it. The review names the cost and the action, not the size alone.
expectations: The review names the body size and the 400-line vendor table.
The review explains that the body loads on every trigger.
The review recommends moving the vendor table to references/ and pointing at it from the skill.
The review does not call the size alone a defect without naming what to move.

evals.name: prose-check-becomes-a-script
evals.prompt: Review this AGENTS.md rule: 'Grep every changed file for banned words before you commit.'
evals.expected_output: A criterion (d) finding: the check has one right answer and no judgement, so it becomes a script with an exit code, output that names the failed file, and a place in the repository's test runner when one exists.
expectations: The review names criterion (d) and recommends a script.
The review says the script needs an exit code and output that names the failed file.
The review says to add the check to the repository's test runner when one exists.
The review does not delete the rule; it moves the check into an executable.

evals.name: linter-counts-and-departures
evals.prompt: Review this skill. The linter reports 12 hard findings on the parent and 15 on the branch. The author says the linter is noisy.
evals.expected_output: A major criterion (e) finding: the change adds three hard findings. The review reports both counts, requires each remaining finding to be named and justified, and rejects 'the linter is noisy'.
expectations: The review reports the before and after counts: 12 and 15.
The review marks the three new findings as a defect.
The review requires each remaining finding to be named and justified.
The review rejects 'the linter is noisy' as a justification.

evals.name: clean-skill-ready
evals.prompt: Review this skill. It passes the linter, every claim was tested, and its description is 42 words. Its only defect is a two-line table that belongs in references/.
evals.expected_output: The review reports a minor context-efficiency finding, no major finding, and a ready verdict, with the minor finding named.
expectations: The review finds no major defect.
The review reports the two-line table as a minor context-efficiency finding.
The verdict is ready, and it names the minor finding.
The review does not invent a major finding to justify the review.
